chapter_note: Aside from a brief hagiographic opener, this chapter is a continuous cosmological-mechanical exposition: how the three wheels are turned and washed, how the waste is deposited in the sea, how the sea giant is formed and sealed with astral impressions, and the threefold function of the giant within the cosmic architecture. No NT citation formulas, no institutional application, and the analogical coin/craftsman comparison remains internal to the system (cosmos→cosmos). The high chapter-level ‘fatigue’ signal is not borne out by clear pastoral grafting here; the main late element is the opening frame.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic hagiographic/dialogue frame (‘Once again… speaks to his disciples’).

paragraphs.core_text: After the Living Spirit constructed things and the worlds, he came up and set himself upon this earth. He gave a sign to the King of Glory, who turned the three wheels and caused the wheels that are found [ ... ] up above all the mountains; he spread forth the wind to them, he breathed on them, he stirred them up, he washed the earth with the waters. And the waste and the accretion of the three vessels, they of water and of darkness and of fire, which had been discharged upon the earth, he gathered them and deposited them in the sea that is within the walls and the vessels; because of this sea waters are salty. For they have received salt and bitterness from the washing out and cleansing of the three vessels.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Process-mechanical cosmology (three wheels; washing/cleansing; deposition of residue in sea) with no appeal to authority or contemporary institutions; impersonal explanatory voice.

paragraphs.core_text: When the Father of Life came, rising in his ascent to the heights, he discharged the wheel of the stars; he washed it out and loosened all the sediment that was in it. He cast it down to this great inner sea like [ ... ] of the mountain. And that waste, the sediment of the washing out of the wheel, he cast it down and mixed it in with the sea waters. Its own thought collected it together; and the thought gathered the waste together in this way. It made it fast and fixed it [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic engineering of the astral wheel and its sediment; ‘thought’ operates as an internal cosmological force, not moral exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: The sea giant had stamped upon him the seal of the seconds and the hours, the seal of the days and months and years, the impression of the stars and the signs of the zodiac [ ... ] He came into existence from them and was discharged from their power and cast into the sea. The images and the seals and aspects and doctrines and counsels of [ ... ] were sealed upon the body of that giant, because he is the residue of them all. Consequently, each star that will shine, and each sign of the zodiac that will turn: of one he shall be its inducement, and of another its confirmation.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic astral-correspondential sealing (time units, stars, zodiac) onto a cosmic being; entirely cosmos→cosmos mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: He was discharged into the sea like this, the way a cloud might discharge rainwater into the midst of the sea. They compelled him totally through the action of the power and the helmsmanship of the angels. He was swept down to the mill, the place where he was constructed in the setting up of the universe; and the sea also conceived him [ ... ] for its part [ ... ] it being his chief sculptor and chief craftsman. It sculpted him in a likeness, he being changed more than the other residue of the sea bodies.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mythic-mechanical formation sequence (discharge, angelic ‘helmsmanship’, cosmic ‘mill’, sea as craftsman). No institutional or paraenetic turn.

paragraphs.core_text: This matter is comparable with a craftsman who might take the stamped impressions of many coins and cast them on the fire, and mould them [to a single] image. These thousands of impressions and thousands of shapes [are perfected] and make a single body [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Internal analogy explaining cosmic formation (many impressions → one body). No Gospel/NT citation formula; functions as correspondential exposition, not later moral application.

paragraphs.core_text: This is also the case with the sea giant, who too was moulded and sculpted by the power of the lust inside him from many doctrines and counsels that belong to the residue of the wheel of the sphere.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the formation mechanism and ties it back to sphere-residue; ‘lust’ functions as an internal cosmological power here, not an exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: The archetype of the giant was constructed for three things.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered structural transition (‘three things’) characteristic of systematic teaching layers.

paragraphs.core_text: The first: That the sphere would be relieved and purified of the burden present in it. In the same way that the ten firmaments were purified and relieved of the burden of the three vessels; so was it also done to the sphere, that it too might be relieved and purified of the burden and the waste inside it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic ‘purification’ described as a mechanical unloading of waste across firmaments/sphere; not ethical/pastoral purification language.

paragraphs.core_text: The second: That he might add a [fetter] and a prison to the wheel and the signs of the zodiac that are bound to it, so that when they wish to go up above, you can find the sea giant dragging them back as by an iron [fetter], and they are unable to go up; and when the powers of the wheel would take a decision on a guileful thing, and it enters their mind to come down to the earth, they are not able to descend because of this stake that is nailed to the wheel upon the [...] of the firmaments. This is one. However, this other one, because of its sleepless watchers that are set over it, it is turned all the time.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic restraining mechanism (fetter/prison/stake; watchers; wheel/zodiac motion control). Minor second-person phrasing (‘you can find’) remains descriptive, not an address to church practice.

paragraphs.core_text: The third thing: That the wind and the water and the fire that gush from the circuit of the sea, and the rivers that flow upon the face of the earth discharging into the sea, and the rainwaters that come to ground, and the waste and rebirth that come down to it; that sea will be a hostel and gathering place for all of these.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third functional purpose, framed as cosmic hydraulics/elemental circulation; ‘hostel and gathering place’ describes cosmic collection, not community institution.

paragraphs.core_text: As for all the power and the life that comes down to the sea, and in the breath that the sea giant will breathe and draw it into him that he might disturb the sea [ ... a] fullness and a [ ... ] becomes between his movement [ ... ] purify; but the sea [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Heavily lacunose, but remains within the same cosmological mechanism (life/power entering sea; giant’s breath; purification process). Dating is less secure due to damage, yet no markers of frame/overlay/pastoral are present.
